$description: SWS design tokens. Three layers: primitive -> semantic -> component. Values are taken from the live production site at sws.somion.ch (measured 2026-09-01): Rubik, indigo #4E4FEB, green #22C55E, near-black #020617, white ground, 8-24px radii. The brand look is pinned by the running product, so this file matches it rather than proposing an alternative. No component token may reference a primitive directly.

primitive.$description: Layer 1. Raw values, sampled from the production site. Never referenced by a component token, and never exported to CSS.

indigo.$description: The brand accent. 500 is the exact value measured on the production Login and Get Started buttons.

slate.$description: Text and chrome. 950 is the production body colour; the mid steps are the greys measured around it.

status.$description: success is the production green, measured at 132 uses across the page.

semantic.$description: Layer 2. Dark mode happens HERE and nowhere else. Each token carries a light and a dark value; the build fails if one theme is missing a token the other declares.

surface-page.$description: The page ground. Near-white with the faintest cool cast, matching production.

surface-raised.$description: Cards. White on near-white, separated by shadow rather than by a border.

surface-raised-2.$description: The second elevation step. White is the ceiling in light, so this equals surface-raised and the step is carried by shadow and border instead. Dark is where it does real work.

scrim.$description: The wash behind a drawer or a modal. Alpha black, like a shadow: absence of light, not a palette colour.

text-disabled.$description: WCAG exempts disabled controls from 1.4.3. Held to the 3:1 non-text bar anyway as an internal rule: a control nobody can read is a control nobody can find.

border-strong.$description: Input borders. Held at a value that clears WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 against both surfaces — see gaps/gap-register.md G10.

action-primary.$description: #4E4FEB, measured on the production primary button

action-subtle-bg.$description: Icon tiles and the announcement pill

action-quiet.$description: Indigo text that has to pass 4.5:1 on white

surface-raised.$description: Lighter than base — depth via light, not shadow

surface-raised-2.$description: One step lighter again. The last legal rung: border-strong on slate.800 measures 3.03:1 and clears SC 1.4.11 by 0.03, and on slate.700 measures 2.14:1 and fails. A third level must be signalled by border and radius, not lightness.

scrim.$description: Heavier than light: a 45% wash over an already-dark page does not separate the drawer from it.

text-primary.$description: Not pure white — pure white fatigues the eye

action-primary.$description: Lifted for dark surfaces. indigo-400 measured 4.39:1 as link text on a dark card.

component.$description: Layer 3. References semantic tokens ONLY. A component token pointing at a primitive is a bug — it makes dark mode impossible.

height-sm.$description: Dense contexts only. Its 44px hit area is declared below and enforced by the gate — see ADR-0004.

height-md.$description: Default. Raised from the Playbook's 40px on 2026-07-29 — see ADR-0002. Do not revert.

height-lg.$description: Production measures its hero buttons at 48px; 52px keeps a readable step above the 44px default.

hit-area.$description: Standalone links. Inline links inside a paragraph inherit the line box and are exempt per SC 2.5.8.

tile-bg.$description: The lavender icon tile behind a card's pictogram, as on production

banner.$description: All four severities. Only danger existed until 2026-09-01, so dist/tokens.css shipped one severity of four while the gate passed all eight checks — the one place a pass covered a real absence. Screen S-05 needs four.

typography.$description: Rubik is the production face, confirmed by computed style on sws.somion.ch. It carries Latin and Arabic in one family, which is why the Arabic and English pages hold the same texture instead of pairing two unrelated faces.

arabic.$description: Rubik ships a full Arabic set, so one family covers both scripts.

rules: Never use a weight below 400 for Arabic — 300 renders Arabic near-illegible on standard displays.
Arabic line-height runs taller than Latin at the same size because of diacritics and below-baseline dots.
German is the width-governing language, not English (+30% and often more). Test every button and column header with German before approving it.
All numerals are Latin (0123) in every context including Arabic UI — decision B4, 2026-09-01.
Tabular figures are mandatory anywhere numbers stack in a column.

tracking.$description: Letter-spacing. The scale above carried size, line-height and weight but no tracking, so every component picked its own — ten distinct values across the client area alone. Four roles cover all of them, and Arabic takes normal everywhere: Arabic letterforms join, so tracking breaks the join.

tight.use: Figures at 30px and up, where the default fit is loose

wide.use: Latin small-caps labels: table heads, nav group labels

label.use: Uppercase labels: eyebrows, table headers, the wordmark strapline. Added because the scale jumped 0.06em to 0.4em and nine real values sat in the gap

widest.use: A code typed one character at a time, where the gap is the point

radius.$description: Measured on production: 4, 6, 8, 12, 16 and full pills all appear. This is the subset the system uses.

rule.$description: Hairline weights for tables and dividers.

shadow.$description: Offset plus soft blur, never a zero-offset halo. Alpha black is deliberate: a shadow is absence of light, not a palette colour.

cta.$description: The one shadow that is a colour rather than an absence of light. Written literally because a shadow token is a composite string, not a colour reference the build can resolve — so it must be re-checked by hand if indigo moves (decision C22).

motion.$description: Exponential ease-out from an already-visible default. Every duration is overridden to 0 under prefers-reduced-motion.

spacing.$description: Base-4 scale. No value outside this scale.

elevation.$description: Elevation, stated once per theme, because the two do not raise a surface the same way. Light has no lightness left above white so it lifts with shadow; dark cannot use shadow — a near-black blur on a near-black ground is invisible — so it lifts with the surface step and spends nothing here. This answers the objection in DESIGN.md: elevation was a language that existed in one theme only, because it was spelled in shadow only.

weight.$description: Weights existed only bound to a type role, so 134 of 143 declarations were raw numbers and the Arabic floor was enforced by eye. 400 is the floor and there is deliberately nothing below it: Arabic letterforms lose their joins.

regular.use: Body text. The floor — nothing lighter exists, in either script

medium.use: A label, or a spec line that should read before its neighbours

semibold.use: A value against its key: prices, counts, table figures

bold.use: Headings, and the register Arabic uses where Latin would use caps

leading.$description: Line height for the cases the type roles do not cover. Role-bound line heights still win where a role applies.

flat.use: A single line that must not add space: a badge, a chip, a count

tight.use: Display and hero, where the roles do not reach

loose.use: Long prose: the knowledge base and the legal pages

size.$description: Widths that are neither spacing nor type: column floors, panel widths, content measures. 62 raw rem literals across 28 distinct values existed before this, plus three locally-invented properties in app.css (--app-side, --app-bar, --dot).

control.use: The 44px touch target as a length (ADR-0002, ADR-0004)

tile.use: The smallest thing that can be a grid cell

field.use: A form control that should not stretch to its container

card.use: The floor a plan or feature card may shrink to before the grid rewraps

column.use: A secondary column beside a main one

table.use: The floor a data table keeps before its wrapper scrolls

prose.use: Running text, where the 62ch measure is not the right tool

document.use: An invoice: the width a page of record wants

shell.use: The outer container. 1200px, matching .shell in world.css

layer.$description: A named stacking order. Before this the stylesheets hand-picked -1, 40, 40, 50, 55, 60, 70, 80 and 100, and nothing stopped a new overlay landing between an existing pair. The gaps are deliberate: room to insert without renumbering.

behind.use: The plotted grid on the page ground, and nothing else

raised.use: A cell or card that lifts above its neighbours

sticky.use: A sticky rail, table header or summary panel

bar.use: The masthead and the client-area top bar

scrim.use: The wash that covers the page behind a drawer

drawer.use: A navigation drawer, above its own scrim

popover.use: The notifications popover and the currency confirm

consent.use: The consent bar. Above everything except a message about itself

toast.use: Nothing may cover it: a saved or copied confirmation, and the skip link — a bypass something can sit on top of is not a bypass

breakpoints.$description: Mobile-first. Most of the Egyptian and Gulf market arrives on a phone. The four device bands define the grid; the content band below them is separate on purpose — those are not devices, they are the widths at which a specific layout stops working, and folding them into the device ladder would move the layout each one exists for.

content.$description: Breakpoints a screen earned. Each names what breaks below it.

compact.use: Below this the order summary and the auth card go single-column

settings.use: The notification preference grid stops being a table: scrolling sideways to reach a toggle is the wrong answer on a settings screen

shell.use: The masthead gives up its inline nav for a drawer; the client-area sidebar goes off-canvas

roomy.use: A wider shell gutter and an uneven dashboard split. The only breakpoint that buys comfort rather than fixing a break

accessibility.$description: Formal commitment is WCAG 2.2 AA (decision I17, resolved 2026-09-01). Two internal rules deliberately exceed AA and are held on purpose: touch-target-min-px 44 is SC 2.5.5 (AAA; the AA bar is 24) and focus-ring-width-px 2 is SC 2.4.13 (AAA; SC 2.4.7 sets no thickness). The gate labels each check with its real SC and level, so AA failures block and AAA shortfalls warn.
